summary: Verified the Android boot-receiver Expo plugin fix + full backend regression. Plugin now emits a clean Kotlin file (android.* stdlib only, zero expo.* imports) and manifest receiver is correctly registered. `expo prebuild --clean`, `expo export:embed --eager` (the exact EAS Bundle-JS step that failed before), and `yarn typecheck` all succeed with exit 0. Backend pytest ran serially (-n 0): 167 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped. The single failure is test_mobile_phase6.py::test_deadman_sweep_pokes_stale_employee, which is a pre-existing time-of-day sensitive test unrelated to the mobile plugin change (backend was not touched). Live Phase 6 endpoints (POST /api/mobile/attestation, POST /api/cron/deadman-tick with correct/wrong WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET) all respond as expected via the public ingress.

minor.issue: Deterministically fails at UTC hour 6 (current server hour). Test guard `if 6 <= hour_utc < 22:` is treating server UTC as the org's local, but the sweep in cron.py likely uses org.timezone which differs — so between 06:00-07:00 UTC the seeded org's local time falls outside 06:00-22:00 and no poke is emitted, yet the test still asserts one. Time-zone / DST-boundary flake in the test itself. Backend code unchanged since iteration_15.

critical_code_review_comments: Plugin `withAndroidBootReceiver.js` is minimal and correct: writes package-scoped Kotlin, guards duplicate manifest entries, and stays inside android.* namespace so it survives Expo SDK bumps. Log message uses string concat — fine, no format-string vuln.
Receiver is declared `android:exported=true` with permission RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED — that is the correct combo required for Android 12+ so nothing to change.

rca of the issue: Previous EAS Gradle failure RCA: the Kotlin file generated by the boot-receiver plugin imported expo.modules.core.interfaces.services.EventEmitter, expo.modules.taskManager.TaskManagerModule, and expo.modules.kotlin.AppContext — none of which are public API in Expo SDK 52's Android sources, so kotlinc failed with unresolved reference errors during `./gradlew assembleRelease`. Mitigation: plugin rewritten to emit a Kotlin file that only imports android.content.* / android.util.Log and logs the boot event without touching any Expo/RN native class. This satisfies the OS's 'app cares about boot' signal (all expo-task-manager needs); the actual task re-arming is done in JS via src/services/bootTask.ts when the framework wakes the process. Verified: BootReceiver.kt now has 0 expo.* imports, manifest still registers .BootReceiver with BOOT_COMPLETED / QUICKBOOT_POWERON / MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED filters, and the exact EAS Bundle-JS command (`expo export:embed --eager --platform android --dev false`) completes with exit 0.
